title: Basic income advocacy and sign appeal decision
subtitle: Goodwill sign appeal, pedestrian crossovers, arts grant policy, economic development funding and the 2023 surplus projection.
overview: Council voted to ask the federal and Ontario governments to create an income-tested guaranteed livable basic income, and to raise Ontario Works and ODSP rates and tie them to inflation. The motion passed {{vote:m9}}. Existing local supports are to keep running while any program is phased in. Council cited income inequality and rising food and housing costs in the region.

Council upheld the Sign Variance Committee's decision on the Goodwill store at 428 King Street North {{vote:m3}}. An attempt to let Goodwill use the freestanding pylon sign failed {{vote:m2}}, so the dimming condition and the removal of a large donation-centre sign stay in place.

Council also approved new Level 2 pedestrian crossover locations {{vote:m6}} and an Arts Grant Policy {{vote:m5}}. It agreed to renew the Waterloo Region Economic Development Corporation partnership, with funding increases to be considered in the 2024-2026 budgets {{vote:m8}}. A 2023 budget update projected small surpluses, with a final allocation report due by May 2024 {{vote:m7}}.

decisions.detail: Council asked the federal and Ontario governments to establish an income-tested basic income, keep existing supports during phase-in, raise and index OW and ODSP rates, and send the resolution to senior governments and municipal bodies.
Council received the staff report and confirmed the Sign Variance Appeal Tribunal's decision on the application for 428 King Street North.
A motion to allow Goodwill signage on the freestanding sign failed, leaving the committee's ban on it in place.
Council approved the crossover locations in the implementation plan and directed that Traffic and Parking By-law 08-77 be updated.

Council approved the draft partnership agreement with the Waterloo Region Economic Development Corporation and directed staff to include increases of $100,000 in 2024, $50,000 in 2025 and $50,000 in 2026 in the 2024-2026 operating budget.
Council approved the Arts Grant Policy as part of the Community Grants Renewal.
Council acknowledged projected 2023 surpluses of about $0.2M in the tax base and $1.1M in the Enterprise budget, and asked for a final allocation report by May 2024.

debate: On the Goodwill sign appeal, the applicant's representative said the pylon panels would otherwise sit as blank illuminated white boxes. They also said the corner and donation-centre signs were needed for visibility and wayfinding, and that the area is fully commercial.

Some councillors questioned the appeal. They noted that the larger corner sign was already approved, that the donation canopy already has signage, and that space on the pylon signs should stay available for a new grocery tenant. Others cited trust in the Sign Variance Committee's trade-offs.

On pedestrian crossovers, councillors raised sightline problems at one proposed site and confusion over two-stage crossings. Staff said every site goes through detailed design and that provincial rules limit single-stage mid-block crossings. Councillors also asked about safety at regional roundabouts and said the crossovers should be reviewed as conditions change.

On the economic development renewal, one councillor called it another cost downloaded to municipalities. A councillor asked why inflation indexing was added, and staff said it is not applied consistently across agreements. The corporation's CEO said federal and provincial program funding is shrinking and uncertain.

Delegates on basic income presented food bank, wage and poverty data, and ways to fund the program. Councillors in support cited health and housing savings, income inequality and local leadership on poverty.
